{{Top|Enemy|Corpus|Corpus|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|Laser Rifle with Corpus safe-guards removed.}} The '''Flux Rifle''' is a {{Faction|Corpus}} laser rifle used by [[Elite Crewman|Elite Crewmen]]. A continuous weapon, the Flux Rifle fires a sustained beam with high {{D|Slash}} damage, enabling it to slice through flesh with ease. It also features a battery that automatically regenerates ammo after the user stops firing for a second. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals primarily {{D|Slash}} damage. *Innate 0.5 meter [[punch through]]. *Does not use ammo pickups; ammo regenerates over time. **Has a '''1''' second delay after the weapon stops firing before regenerating ammo. Then, regenerates '''40''' ammo per second; takes '''1.25''' seconds to regenerate a fully depleted battery excluding the delay. **Does not benefit from mods that increase [[Ammo#Ammo Maximum|maximum ammo]], due to lack of an ammo pool. **Does not receive benefit from reload-triggered mods such as {{M|Spring-Loaded Chamber}}. *Can use the Flux Rifle-exclusive {{M|Flux Overdrive}} mod. {{Advantages|class=Rifle|trigger=Held| *Pinpoint [[accuracy]]. *Consumes 0.5 ammo per tick of damage. }} {{Disadvantages|class=Rifle|trigger=Held| *Damage ramps up from 25% to 100% over 0.6 seconds when firing. After firing stops for 0.8 seconds, the damage decays back to 25% over 2 seconds. *Thin continuous short range laser, requires precise aiming. **Staggered opponents may 'jump' out of user's crosshair. *Limited range of 30 meters. }} {{WeaponComparison|Tenet Flux Rifle}} ==Acquisition== The Flux Rifle's blueprint can be [[research]]ed from the [[Research/Energy Lab|Energy Lab]] in the [[dojo]]. {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} This weapon can be sold for {{cc|7,500}}. ==Notes== *Because the 50 shots count as part of a single magazine rather than an ammo pool, mods like {{M|Ammo Drum}} have no effect. *Can dismember and slice enemies, making it easier to cut through a line of enemies instead of firing at their corpses prematurely. **This also helps with [[Desecrate|Desecrating]] corpses. *As of [[Update 9]], the laser graphic now lines up properly with the target reticle. ==Tips== *Similar to [[Rampart]]s and all [[Archgun]]s, ammo starts to automatically regenerate after '''1''' second of not firing the weapon. This regeneration delay is affected by reload speed mods like {{M|Fast Hands}}. The regeneration rate is 40 ammo per second. **The reload speed can also be increased by using a Toxin-based {{A|Elemental Ward}} or being under the effect of {{A|Speed}} or {{A|Penance}}. *The Flux Rifle has a high chance of cutting corpses into pieces, making it an ideal candidate for a {{A|Desecrate}} {{WF|Nekros}} to bring along, as the game considers the cut corpses as separate entities, essentially giving multiple corpses to desecrate from a single enemy and thus yielding more chances to create more drops. *{{M|Metal Auger}} and/or {{M|Shred}} makes the Flux Rifle much better for dealing with crowds; simply line yourself up so you hit multiple enemies at once to save ammo. *When compared with {{Weapon|Tenet Flux Rifle}}, it is easy to assume that it is a direct upgrade. However, since the normal Flux Rifle is a continuous weapon, the [[multishot]] mechanics associated with beams all apply here. This means it is potentially possible to exceed the status proc rate of its variant (especially with {{M|Galvanized Chamber}}). While the variant has many benefits over the base version, both have potential for different reasons. ==Trivia== *The Flux Rifle was the first rifle that did not follow the [[Corpus]] weapon naming convention; typically a Latin word with two syllables ending in an "a". Others include the {{Weapon|Detron}} and {{Weapon|Amprex}}. *The Flux Rifle was originally meant to be a [[Grineer]] weapon, as shown in the [[Codex]] art gallery. *When initially introduced, the Flux Rifle's description was ''"FLUX RIFLE"'', presumably a developer oversight. *The Flux Rifle has a smaller version in the form of the {{Weapon|Spectra}}, introduced in [[Update 9]]. *The beam of the Flux Rifle bears cosmetic similarity to the [[Orokin Void|Orokin Tower]] Death Orb laser beams. **It is likely that both this gun and the [[Fusion MOA]]'s main weapon were attempts to replicate this technology. *The Flux Rifle itself was never used by the Corpus until [[Operation: Arid Fear]] introduced [[Elite Crewman|Elite Crewmen]], several months after this gun was added. *Up until {{ver|11.3.3}}, {{M|Speed Trigger}}, {{M|Shred}}, {{M|Critical Delay}} and {{M|Vile Precision}} (all of which influence fire rate one way or another) had little (if any) impact on the rate at which the Flux Rifle consumed ammunition. This also held true for other continuous-fire weapons at the time ({{Weapon|Ignis}}, {{Weapon|Synapse}}, etc.) ==Bugs== *While using [[Shade]], holding down the fire button and then proceeding close to enemies will cloak you, and you will continue to be cloaked until your magazine is drained and you must reload. This tactic uses ammo very quickly but may be useful against heavy opponents as you can inflict heavy damage without them retaliating. If you wish to use this tactic, equip {{M|Magazine Warp}} and/or {{M|Wildfire}} to increase the duration of the time spent cloaked before having to reload. *During a solo mission when the game is paused while firing the Flux Rifle, one can see both the flash and beam of the gun blinking. ==Media== 2013-11-22_00002.jpg|Flux Rifle default stats damage type post-11.0.4 Hotfix Flux Rifle Arsenal.png|Flux Rifle when Equipped in the Arsenal Flux RIfle Arsenal 2.png Flux Rifle Arsenal 3.png {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|uuSoGrvlpbM|size=300px}} }} {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|33}} *The following weapons can now be found in their corresponding categories in the Arsenal when searching using the tag “Battery”: **Flux Rifle {{ver|32.0.2}} ;Ammo Changes & Review: When we were reviewing ammo acquisition as a whole for Update 32, we felt weapons with Ammo Regen Rate Overrides, or “Battery,” in particular, needed a place within the ecosystem of change we had established. That said, upon review of feedback, we recognize we were a bit heavy-handed with the changes we made to Battery weapons. We have restored their original values for the time being while we reassess how we can better approach these weapons. We have restored the original values for the following weapons: *Flux Rifle: **Returned ammo regen rate to 40/s from 24/s {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapons with Ammo Regen Rates Overrides:''' *Flux Rifle: From 40/s to 24/s {{ver|30.5}} *Updated Flux Rifle muzzle FX. *Fixed the Flux Rifle beam’s impact sounds. {{ver|30.3}} *Fixed issues with the Flux Rifle’s FX. {{ver|27.0.7}} *Fixed Flux Rifle not recharging correctly. {{ver|24.5}} *Fixed hearing Headshot sounds when firing the Flux Rifle. {{ver|22.20}} *PBR treatment. {{ver|22.14}} *Fixed Beam weapons not being able to damage enemies (alive but in a ragdolled state) when being affected by certain ‘crowd control’ Abilities. *Damage now ramps up over 0.6 seconds and after moving off target there is a delay of 0.8 seconds before it starts to decay over 2 seconds. *All Beam weapons now start their Damage ramp up at 20% (instead of 10%). *The Multishot chance should now apply more consistently with Beam weapons. *Fixed Beam weapons continuously firing when quick Meleeing. *Tweaked Flux Rifle controller rumble on recharge. {{ver|22.13.4}} *Increased the Beam weapon Damage ramp up time from 0.8 to 1 second. *Fixed Beam weapon Damage ramp up not happening per target. {{ver|22.13.3}} *Perfect accuracy and high fire rate is balanced by limited range and damage ramping up from 10% to 100% over 0.8 seconds when firing and decays back to 10% over 1 second after stopping. *Damage changed from 22.6 Physical per second to 22 Physical per tick. *Physical damage changed from 10% Impact, 10% Puncture and 90% Slash to 0% Impact, 22% Puncture and 78% Slash. *Fire Rate increased from 10 to 12. *Status Chance changed from 25% per sec to 24% per tick of damage. *Critical chance increased from 5% to 10%. *Ammunition converted to Battery with 50 capacity, 1 sec recharge delay and 40 regen rate. *Range increased from 25m to 30m. *Added 0.5m Punch Through. *Ammo consumption decreased from 1.0 to 0.5 per tick of damage. *Aimed Zoom reduced from 2.23x to 1.8x. *The Flux Rifle has a new battery charge up and fully charged sound to go with it’s beam rework! {{ver|19.5}} *Reduced Flux Rifle magazine capacity from 200 to 30 in '''Conclave'''. {{ver|19.4.2}} *Flux Rifle riven disposition increased. {{ver|The Index Preview}} *Flux Rifle can now be used in Conclave! {{ver|15.11}} *Fixed visual issue with Flux Rifle laser beam appearance. {{ver|15.10.1}} *Fixed the Flux Rifle's material not using the correct energy color. {{ver|14.2}} *Flux Rifle: **More Ammo efficient. **More base ammo in clips. **Faster fire rate. **Damage Increased. {{ver|12}} *Flux Rifle now has improved damage and proc rate. {{ver|11.3.3}} *Fixed in-game stats for weapons that fire continuously (Flux, etc). Made fire-rate mods actually increase damage output and ammo consumption rate for these weapons (not only is this intuitively what you would expect it's important to maintain the balance for corrupted mods like Critical Delay). {{ver|11.0.4}} *Flux Rifle adjustments to not be pure Slash damage. {{ver|11}} *Fixed issue that allowed spectators to fire the Flux Rifle while spectating in Conclave. {{ver|10.3.2}} *Fix for Flux Rifle not being able to damage reactor cores or Orokin death orbs. **Also fixes not being able to pop Saryn's venom orbs. {{ver|9.6.1}} *Improved visual effects for Flux Rifle beam. {{ver|9.6}} *Flux Rifle energy beam is now affected by Energy Colour! {{ver|9.4.1}} *Flux Rifle with Multishot crash fixes and over-the-top corpse destruction. {{ver|9.4}} *Fix for Flux Rifle not being able to damage ragolled enemies on client. {{ver|9.3}} *Smaller radius on impact sounds for the Flux Rifle. {{ver|9}} *Flux Rifle – damage and fire rate buff. {{ver|8.1.2}} *Fixed Flux Rifle showing a clip size of 1.$ in the arsenal. {{ver|8.1}} *Increase max length of Flux Rifle Beam. {{ver|8.0.7.1}} *Increased fire distance on the Flux Rifle. {{ver|8}} *Introduced. }} {{ver/Lu|25.0.8}} ==See Also== *{{Weapon|Tenet Flux Rifle}}, the [[Tenet]] counterpart of this weapon. *{{Weapon|Spectra}}, the side arm version of the Flux Rifle. *[[Elite Crewman]], a Corpus unit that uses this weapon. {{ResearchNav}} {{WeaponNav}} [[de:Flux]] [[es:Rifle de flujo]] [[fr:Fusil à Flux]] [[pt:Flux Rifle]] [[Category:Weapons]] [[Category:Primary Weapons]] [[Category:Assault Rifle]] [[Category:Corpus Weapons]] [[Category:Slash Damage Weapons]] [[Category:Continuous Weapons]] [[Category:Battery Weapons]] [[Category:Corpus]] [[Category:Research]] [[Category:Update 8]] [[Category:Augmented Weapons]] [[uk:Потокова гвинтівка]]

**The actual net damage loss when combined with a maxed Point Blank is 7.9%.
**The actual net damage loss when combined with a maxed {{M|Primed Point Blank}} is 5.7%.

By default it fires silent {{D|Electricity}} pulses at close range akin to the {{Weapon|Arca Plasmor}}, but via [[Alternate Fire]] it can be converted into an automatic weapon that shoots a rapid stream of lightning at a distance. The mode-switching is sped up when used by Wisp. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals primarily {{D|Electricity}} damage. *Semi-auto mode: **Shots have a guaranteed {{D|Impact}} proc to enemies up to 9 meters. ***Distance is affected by [[Projectile Speed]]. **Projectiles have a thickness of 1 meter. *Does not use ammo pickups; ammo regenerates over time. **Has a '''1''' second delay after the weapon stops firing before regenerating ammo. Then, regenerates '''30''' ammo per second; takes '''2''' seconds to regenerate a fully depleted battery excluding the delay. **Does not receive benefit from reload-triggered mods such as {{M|Spring-Loaded Chamber}}. *[[Alternate Fire]] mode-switching is '''not''' instantaneous and has an animation of '''1''' second ('''0.5''' seconds when wielded by {{WF|Wisp}}.) {{Advantages| *Semi-auto mode: **Innate 3 meter [[punch through]] against bodies. **[[Silent]]. *Full-auto mode: **Hitscan and pinpoint [[accuracy]]. *{{M|Heavy Caliber}}'s accuracy penalty is minimal on this weapon. }} {{Disadvantages| *Semi-auto mode: **Has linear damage falloff from 100% to 33.33% from 10m to 20m target distance (distances are affected by [[Projectile Speed]]). **Limited range of 20 meters (can be increased with [[Projectile Speed]] mods). **Consumes 10 ammo per shot. **Has a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] multiplier of 1x. **Innate [[punch through]] does not apply to surfaces if hitting with the central portion of the projectile, requiring [[punch through]] mods. *Full-auto mode: **Shots are alarming. }} {{WeaponComparison|Fulmin Prime}} ==Acquisition== The Fulmin's blueprint can be purchased from the [[Market]]. {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} It can be sold for '''7,500'''. ==Notes== *When wielded by {{WF|Wisp}}/{{WF|Wisp Prime}}, the [[Alternate Fire]] mode-switching animation is decreased to '''0.5''' seconds. *Being categorized as an assault rifle, Fulmin can't be used for "Shotgun Only" Sorties (despite having pulse-shotgun characteristics). ==Tips== *This weapon benefits from guaranteed {{D|Slash}} status effect mods: **Due to its high [[critical chance]] and [[critical multiplier]], it pairs well with {{M|Hunter Munitions}}, which extends to both primary and secondary fire, and works at its full effective range. **Due to its semi auto fire guaranteeing {{D|Impact}} procs, and having a low rate of fire (below 2.5), Fulmin pairs particularly well with {{M|Internal Bleeding}}. However, it will only have an effect at the range at which Impact procs are applied, which is shorter than it's effective range; full auto fire does not benefit from this mod at all. **Despite both these mods technically being slottable at once, the procs caused by them don't stack. *{{M|Heavy Caliber}}'s accuracy loss has minimal effect on this weapon in either fire mode. ==Trivia== *Fulmin is derived from ''[[wiktionary:fulmen|fulmen]]'', the Latin word for lightning. {{Codex|Wield a storm. Fulmin Prime's electric rounds switch between lightning beams and short-range bursts. Wisp quickly swaps between each mode with her elemental prowess.}}
'''Fulmin Prime''' is the [[Prime]]d counterpart of the {{Weapon|Fulmin}} rifle, with increased [[Magazine Size]], faster [[Reload]] delay, improvements to the semi-automatic damage and [[Status Chance]], and full-auto [[Critical Chance]]. Fulmin Prime was released alongside {{WF|Wisp Prime}} and {{Weapon|Gunsen Prime}}.

==Characteristics==
*This weapon deals primarily {{D|Electricity}} damage.
*Semi-auto mode:
**Shots have a guaranteed {{D|Impact}} proc to enemies up to 9 meters.
***Distance is affected by [[Projectile Speed]].
**Projectiles have a thickness of 1 meter.
*Does not use ammo pickups; ammo regenerates over time.
**Has a '''0.7''' second delay after the weapon stops firing before regenerating ammo. Then, regenerates '''40''' ammo per second; takes '''2''' seconds to regenerate a fully depleted battery excluding the delay.
**Does not receive benefit from reload-triggered mods such as {{M|Spring-Loaded Chamber}}.
*[[Alternate Fire]] mode-switching is '''not''' instantaneous and has an animation of '''1''' second ('''0.5''' seconds when wielded by {{WF|Wisp}}/{{WF|Wisp Prime}}.)

{{Advantages|
*Semi-auto mode:
**Innate 3 meter [[punch through]] against bodies.
**[[Silent]].
*Full-auto mode:
**Hitscan and pinpoint [[accuracy]].
*{{M|Heavy Caliber}}'s accuracy penalty is minimal on this weapon.
}}

{{Disadvantages|
*Semi-auto mode:
**Has linear damage falloff from 100% to 33.33% from 10m to 20m target distance (distances are affected by [[Projectile Speed]]).
**Limited range of 20 meters (can be increased with [[Projectile Speed]] mods).
**Consumes 10 ammo per shot.
**Has a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] multiplier of 1x.
**Innate [[punch through]] does not apply to surfaces if hitting with the central portion of the projectile, requiring [[punch through]] mods.
*Full-auto mode:
**Shots are alarming.
}}
